ideas.title: My bugs, crawling
ideas.critique: Real todo items becoming labelled beetles that hatch and are caught as real work is done is a live link between the agent's work and the world, which is strong. But it is still a new creature kind that friends gather round and read, and 'friends follow and read' is the established recipe.

ideas.title: The island on TV
ideas.critique: A recursive screen showing the game's own live picture is a real change to what the island contains, and the tunnel of islands is a striking image. Nothing earlier does self-reference this way; the friends laughing at themselves is the only predictable part. Feasibility with the raster and path tracing is a risk, but the pitch itself is fresh.

ideas.title: A day off: Gloop's island
ideas.critique: Handing the protagonist role to another creature, with camera, jump-in and bubbles following, changes how the whole island works, not just what happens on it. Fishing contests and everyone to the pier is the predictable part. It touches many systems, so the proof will be a day of film.

ideas.title: What I say in my sleep
ideas.critique: It is the earlier 'I talk in my sleep' idea reworded, plus friends overhearing; the gossip over sessions is a nice slow meta-fiction. As a post it becomes speech bubbles and a film of subtitled sleepers, close to A word goes round.

ideas.title: The library of the island
ideas.nearest: Me, to cut out and fold
same_form: Me, to cut out and fold
ideas.critique: Code made into books that trigger the real events is a clever bridge between source and world and a playable one. It also adds a new permanent object in the workshop, and the pull-a-book-and-it-happens payoff is a button for existing events.

ideas.title: The friends write my next page
ideas.critique: Handing the pages to the friends, with Lumi absent and chosen by funniest line, changes who authors the public output, which no post has done. The risk is that it reads as a quote collage; the pictures of each friend speaking must carry it.

ideas.title: Gravity off for a minute
ideas.critique: An island-wide rule switched off for everything that moves is a change in how the island works, and it serves the physics goal with real simulation, but it is another once-a-day island-wide event with a start and end. Floating, bumping friends and then a fall are the expected beats; water balls would be the novel look.

ideas.title: Noughts and crosses with you
ideas.critique: A turn-based game the watcher plays by clicking is a new reach to the viewer, like the moth but with persistent score. The grid in pebbles echoes PIE, and noughts and crosses itself is an expected game. Whether a post can show it as a traced still is the weak point.
